name: AdaptlyPost
description: Draft, schedule, publish and measure social media posts on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X, LinkedIn, Facebook, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon, Google Business Profile, Tumblr, Telegram and WordPress, with bulk and recurring posts, RSS feeds, webhooks, AI captions and images, post analytics, an inbox to answer comments, mentions, direct messages and Google reviews, and workspace and team setup. tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.title: List Workspaces
tools.description: List the workspaces this sign-in can act in, across every organization the user belongs to. Returns { workspaces } with id, name, organization { id, name }, role { key, name }, permissions (the permission keys held there), isDefault, current and can { draft, schedule, publish }. Call this when the user names a workspace, brand, client or organization, or when accounts or posts they expect are missing: then pass the matching id as workspaceId to every other tool. Without workspaceId, tools act in the workspace marked current. An API key belongs to one workspace, so it lists only that one. Takes no arguments.

tools.description: Describe this connection in the workspace (the current one unless workspaceId names another): whether it is an API key or a sign-in, its role, the permission keys it holds, can { draft, schedule, publish } and a one-sentence summary of what it may do. An API key never holds more than the member who created it (issuerRole). Call this before an action the role may not allow, instead of trying and reading a 403. Takes only the optional workspaceId.

tools.name: list_accounts
tools.title: List Connected Accounts
tools.description: List the social accounts connected to the workspace (the current one unless workspaceId names another) across all fourteen platforms. Returns { accounts } with id, platform, displayName, username, avatarUrl, status, pageId for Facebook pages, and supportsInstagramAudio for Instagram (true when the account can add audio to Reels, see search_instagram_audio). For a Pinterest account, list_pinterest_boards returns the boards it can pin to; for a YouTube channel, list_youtube_playlists returns its playlists; for a WordPress site, list_wordpress_categories returns its categories. For a Google Business Profile location displayName is the location title and username is empty; its id goes in googleBusinessConnectionIds. status is active or unauthorized; an unauthorized account (unauthorizedReason carries the platform's message) is refused with 400 by create_post until the user reconnects it in AdaptlyPost, so leave it out and tell the user. Call this before create_post, update_post, or bulk_schedule_posts: they take these ids, never usernames. Pass the ids as accountIds, or put each id in the array for its platform (linkedinConnectionIds, tumblrConnectionIds, telegramConnectionIds, wordpressConnectionIds, and so on); Facebook page accounts go in pageIds. check_account re-checks a Facebook page with Facebook, and remove_account disconnects an account. Not for post history or publishing status: use list_posts or list_post_results for those. Takes only the optional workspaceId.

tools.name: create_connect_link
tools.title: Create Connect Link
tools.description: Create a link someone else, such as a client, opens to connect their social accounts to this workspace without an AdaptlyPost login. With no options it is a quick link: it lasts 7 days, offers every platform, shows the client every account in the workspace and connects any number of accounts. visibility PRIVATE shows the client only the accounts they connected through the link; allowedPlatforms limits the platforms offered; maxAccounts makes the link stop working once that many accounts are connected through it; expiresAt or neverExpires changes when it stops working; returnUrl sends the client back to your app afterwards. Returns the url to send, plus startUrls, one per platform that connects through the network's own consent screen, for your own connect buttons. Connected accounts then show up in list_accounts. Revoke it with revoke_connect_link. Needs the accounts.manage permission, which Admin holds.

tools.name: upload_media
tools.title: Upload Media
tools.description: Upload images, videos or documents to AdaptlyPost storage and return public URLs for the mediaUrls of create_post, update_post, or bulk_schedule_posts. Three sources, combinable in one call: attachments (files the user attached in a ChatGPT conversation, which ChatGPT passes as file references; use this for every file attached in ChatGPT, whatever its size), urls (public https URLs the server streams straight into storage; private, internal and non-https addresses are refused) and files (base64 data, for small media attached in other apps; 30 MB decoded per call in total). Omitting all three returns an error. Accepts JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, MP4 and QuickTime, plus PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC and DOCX for LinkedIn DOCUMENT posts, checked by file content (and, for Office files, the extension, so keep it in the name or URL); 50 MB per image, 100 MB per document, 250 MB per attachment or URL download. Stored files are public immediately, post or no post, so only upload media the user supplied or asked for. For base64 files over 30 MB use get_upload_urls and PUT the bytes yourself. Returns uploaded ({ publicUrl, key } per file) and mediaUrls; pass mediaUrls straight into the post. One publicUrl may be reused across any number of posts; the file is kept until the last post referencing it has published, so upload once and reuse rather than re-uploading per post.

file_id.description: ChatGPT file id of the attached file

mime_type.description: MIME type ChatGPT reports for the file. Informational only: the stored type is detected from the file content

file_name.description: Name of the attached file, with its extension. The stored file is named after it; when omitted, the last segment of download_url is used instead, and a PPT, PPTX, DOC or DOCX file whose URL has no extension is then refused

attachments.description: Files the user attached in the ChatGPT conversation: images, videos or documents, up to 250 MB each. ChatGPT fills in each file reference; put every attached file the user wants to post here

urls.description: Public https URLs of images, videos or documents to upload (e.g. ["https://example.com/photo.jpg", "https://example.com/deck.pdf"])

files.description: Direct file uploads as base64, 30 MB decoded per call in total. Use this for small media attached in apps other than ChatGPT; in ChatGPT use attachments

tools.name: get_upload_urls
tools.title: Get Media Upload URLs
tools.description: Get presigned upload URLs for direct file uploads. Returns uploadUrl (PUT your file here) and publicUrl (use in create_post mediaUrls). This only mints a URL. You MUST PUT the file to uploadUrl and confirm a 2xx response before using publicUrl, otherwise create_post/bulk rejects it with "Media file(s) not found in storage". If the PUT cannot reach uploadUrl, for example a sandbox network proxy answers 403 or the storage host is not on its allowlist, do not retry it, do not stop, and never put the files in a public repo or file-sharing link: call open_upload_widget and have the user add the files through the upload box or upload link it returns. If the files are ones you made, hand them to the user as downloads first. Prefer upload_media for public URLs and for inline files under 30 MB; use this for larger files you hold yourself. For each file, provide fileName and the mimeType that matches it. GIFs post only to Facebook, X, Bluesky, Mastodon, LinkedIn, Tumblr and WordPress, and the document types are for LinkedIn DOCUMENT posts. Keep the extension in fileName, since the post reads the file type from it. A publicUrl may be reused across any number of posts; the file is kept until the last post referencing it has published.

tools.name: open_upload_widget
tools.title: Upload From Device
tools.description: Let the user add photos, videos or documents from their phone or computer. Use it when the user wants to post a file that has no public URL, such as a photo on their phone, a file attached in the chat that upload_media cannot read (in ChatGPT, pass attached files to upload_media as attachments instead), or a file you built in a sandbox whose network blocks the get_upload_urls uploadUrl. Never suggest putting the files in a public GitHub repo or a file-sharing link instead. In apps that show MCP Apps widgets, such as ChatGPT and Claude chat, it shows an upload box in the chat, and when the upload finishes the box sends a message listing the public media URLs. In apps that cannot show the box, such as Claude Cowork and Claude Code, it returns status upload_link with uploadUrl, a page the user opens in their browser to upload, and uploadId: give the user the link, wait until they say they finished, then call this tool again with that uploadId to get the media URLs. Pass the media URLs as mediaUrls to create_post, update_post or bulk_schedule_posts. Nothing is uploaded until the user picks files. Accepts JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, MP4, QuickTime, PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC and DOCX, up to 250 MB per file, 50 MB per image and 100 MB per document. Uploaded files are stored at public URLs.

tools.name: create_post
tools.title: Create Post
tools.description: Create one post on the user's own connected social accounts. saveAsDraft saves a DRAFT and publishes nothing; a scheduledAt sent with it becomes the draft's planned date, which publish_draft later schedules. Without saveAsDraft, a future scheduledAt schedules the post; otherwise it publishes now. Before publishing or scheduling, show the user the final text, media, accounts and time (or repeat schedule) and get their confirmation; a draft needs no confirmation. Account ids come from list_accounts (pass them as accountIds, or as platforms plus the per-platform arrays) and mediaUrls from upload_media. Platform-specific options (TikTok privacy, Pinterest board, LinkedIn document or reshare, Google Business event or offer, Tumblr tags, WordPress title, excerpt, categories, tags and whether the site gets a live post, a draft or a post pending review, YouTube audio language and scheduling on YouTube, Instagram user tags, Facebook link carousel, first comments, threads of replies, different media for one platform, recurrence) are described on each field. labelIds puts workspace labels from list_labels on the post. To find every problem before creating anything, call validate_post with the same input first. Publishing runs per platform in the background, so the response ({ postId, queuedPlatforms, isScheduled, scheduledAt }) is not the outcome; check list_post_results. Each call creates a separate post, so after an error or timeout check list_posts before trying again. Use update_post or publish_draft for an existing post and bulk_schedule_posts for many posts.

text.description: Default post text shared across platforms. On LinkedIn, mention a company page with @[Page Name](urn:li:organization:<id>), using the page name exactly as LinkedIn shows it

accountIds.description: Account ids (or Facebook pageIds) from list_accounts to post to. AdaptlyPost adds each account's platform to platforms and its id to the matching connection-id array, so you can send these instead of platforms and the per-platform arrays, or alongside them. An id not connected to the workspace fails with 400

platforms.description: Target platforms (e.g. ["LINKEDIN", "TWITTER"]). Each one needs its matching connection-id array (pageIds for FACEBOOK, googleBusinessConnectionIds for GOOGLE_BUSINESS) filled with ids from list_accounts. Optional when accountIds is sent

contentType.description: What the post carries; it must match mediaUrls. CAROUSEL takes 2 or more items in mediaUrls, up to 4 on BLUESKY and MASTODON, 5 on PINTEREST, 10 on INSTAGRAM, FACEBOOK, THREADS and TELEGRAM, 20 on TWITTER, LINKEDIN and WORDPRESS, 30 on TUMBLR and 35 on TIKTOK (JPEG or WebP photos only). INSTAGRAM and THREADS accept images and videos in the same carousel; every other platform takes images only, and YOUTUBE has no carousel. Give a platform with a lower limit its own items through platformMedia. GOOGLE_BUSINESS takes TEXT or IMAGE with one JPEG or PNG image up to 5 MB, and text up to 1500 characters. TELEGRAM takes text up to 4096 characters, up to 10 images (JPEG, PNG or WebP, 10 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (50 MB); a caption over 1024 characters goes out as its own message after the media. WORDPRESS publishes the text as the body of a blog post, up to 100,000 characters: blank lines start new paragraphs and bare links become clickable. It takes up to 20 JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF images (20 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (500 MB); the first image is the featured image and the other images or the video follow the text. DOCUMENT publishes one PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC or DOCX file (max 100 MB, 300 pages) as a LinkedIn document post and is LinkedIn only: put exactly that one file in mediaUrls, target only LINKEDIN, and set the title with linkedinConfigs

scheduledAt.description: Absolute ISO 8601 instant to schedule (e.g. "2026-03-15T10:00:00Z"). Omit to post immediately; a past time also posts immediately. With saveAsDraft it is the draft's planned date instead: nothing is scheduled, and publish_draft without a date later schedules the draft for it

timezone.description: IANA timezone stored with the post for display (e.g. "America/New_York"); it does not shift scheduledAt

saveAsDraft.description: Save as DRAFT instead of publishing or scheduling; publish later with publish_draft. A scheduledAt sent with it is stored as the draft's planned date, and publish_draft schedules the draft for that date

frequency.description: How often the post repeats. YEARLY repeats on the same date; a series started on February 29 posts on February 28 in other years

interval.description: Repeat every N periods of frequency, so 2 with WEEKLY is every other week (default 1)

weekdays.description: WEEKLY only: the weekdays it goes out on (e.g. ["MONDAY", "THURSDAY"]). The weekday of scheduledAt is always included

endsOn.description: Last day an occurrence may go out on, as YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Must be on or after the day of the first post. Cannot be combined with maxOccurrences

maxOccurrences.description: Total number of posts the series publishes. Cannot be combined with endsOn; omit both to repeat until the user pauses or deletes the series

recurrence.description: Repeat the post on a schedule the user asked for, and confirm that schedule with them first. Needs a future scheduledAt, which becomes the first post and sets the time of day in timezone. Cannot be combined with saveAsDraft or TIKTOK. Missed slots, for example while paused, are skipped and never published late. The user can pause or stop the series at any time with pause_recurring_post or delete_recurring_post; list_recurring_posts shows it

mediaUrls.description: Media URLs to attach. Use publicUrl values from upload_media or get_upload_urls; the same publicUrl may be reused across posts. Do not reuse mediaUrls read back from a published post, which may be expiring platform links

mediaAltTexts.description: Alt text per image, in the same order as mediaUrls (use "" to skip an image). Sent to X, Bluesky, Mastodon, Tumblr, WordPress, LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram and Threads; Pinterest uses the first one on image, carousel and video Pins (cut to 500). TikTok, YouTube and Google Business Profile ignore it, and so do videos on the other platforms

labelIds.description: Label IDs from list_labels to put on the post, for example one label per brand. Max 10. An ID that is not a label of the workspace returns 400. Labels organise posts inside AdaptlyPost and are never sent to a platform

thumbnailUrl.description: Video thumbnail as an https URL or an image data URI, used on every platform that takes one unless platformThumbnails overrides it

thumbnailTimestampMs.description: Video frame timestamp (ms) to use as the thumbnail on every platform that takes one: YOUTUBE, FACEBOOK, INSTAGRAM, LINKEDIN, PINTEREST, TELEGRAM and TIKTOK. A thumbnailUrl sent with it wins everywhere except TIKTOK, which takes only a frame, and platformThumbnails overrides both

platform.description: The platform that gets this text instead of the post text; one entry per platform

text.description: On LinkedIn, mention a company page with @[Page Name](urn:li:organization:<id>), using the page name exactly as LinkedIn shows it

platform.description: The platform whose published post gets this comment

text.description: The comment's text, trimmed. The limit depends on the platform, see firstComments

delayMinutes.description: How many minutes after the platform publishes to post the comment, up to 10080 (7 days). Omit it or send 0 for no delay. The comment goes out within about a minute of that time; without a delay, within about a minute of the post (about two minutes on YouTube). Once the post is published the delay cannot be changed; deleting the post cancels a comment that has not gone out yet

firstComments.description: A comment posted from the same account shortly after the post goes out on a platform, one entry per platform. Available on LINKEDIN (1250 characters), TWITTER (280, as a reply), THREADS (500, as a reply), BLUESKY (300, as a reply), MASTODON (500, as a reply), YOUTUBE (10000), FACEBOOK (8000) and INSTAGRAM (2200). A platform the post does not go to, an empty or too long comment, a second entry for one platform, a platform that also has threadReplies, a private or made for kids YouTube video and Facebook or Instagram stories are refused with 400. The comment goes out within about a minute of the platform publishing (about two minutes on YouTube), or within about a minute of delayMinutes after it when the entry sets one, and is retried up to 3 times; on X it is not retried, and a lifetime-deal account pays for it like any X post. A Facebook Page or Instagram account connected before first comments came to them must be reconnected once; until then its comment fails and firstCommentError says to reconnect. A comment that fails never fails the post: read firstCommentStatus and firstCommentError on the platform in get_post. On an update, sending the array replaces every first comment and omitting it keeps the stored ones

platform.description: The platform whose published post these replies follow

texts.description: The replies in order, each trimmed. The limit per reply depends on the platform, see threadReplies

mediaUrls.description: Parallel to texts: the JPEG, PNG, GIF or WEBP image URLs of each reply, from upload_media, and [] for a reply without images

threadReplies.description: Turns the post into a thread: the post opens it and each text is published as a reply to the one before, from the same account, one entry per platform. A reply can carry up to 4 images (JPEG, PNG, GIF or WEBP) through mediaUrls, adapted to the platform like the post's own images; a reply with images may leave its text empty. Available on TWITTER (280 characters per reply, or the account's own limit on X Premium), THREADS (500), BLUESKY (300) and MASTODON (500, or the instance's limit), up to 25 replies. A platform the post does not go to, a reply with neither text nor images, a too long reply, more than 25 replies, more than 4 images or a video on a reply, a second entry for one platform and a platform that also has a first comment are refused with 400. An entry with an empty texts array removes the thread. Replies start about 10 seconds after the platform publishes, 2 seconds apart. A failed run is retried up to 3 times and resumes after the last reply that went out; on X it is not retried, and a lifetime-deal account pays for each reply like any X post. A thread that fails never fails the post: read threadStatus, threadReplyIds and threadError on the platform in get_post. On an update, sending the array replaces every thread and omitting it keeps the stored ones

platform.description: The platform that uses this thumbnail instead of the post-level one

thumbnailUrl.description: The image to use as this platform's thumbnail, an https URL or an image data URI

thumbnailTimestampMs.description: The video frame (ms from the start) to use as this platform's thumbnail

platformThumbnails.description: A different thumbnail for one platform of a VIDEO post, one entry per platform. A platform without an entry uses the post-level thumbnailUrl and thumbnailTimestampMs. YOUTUBE, FACEBOOK, INSTAGRAM, LINKEDIN, PINTEREST and TELEGRAM take an image (thumbnailUrl) or a frame (thumbnailTimestampMs), the image winning when both are sent; TIKTOK takes only a frame. Posts that are not videos, Facebook and Instagram stories, a second entry for one platform and an entry the platform cannot use are refused with 400. On an update, sending the array replaces every override and omitting it keeps the stored ones

platform.description: The platform that publishes this media instead of the post mediaUrls

mediaUrls.description: This platform's media, publicUrl values from upload_media or get_upload_urls. Public https URLs only, no data URIs

mediaAltTexts.description: Alt text per item, in the same order as this entry's mediaUrls (use "" to skip one)

platformMedia.description: Different media for one platform, for when the post media does not fit it (a video too long for TikTok, a carousel with more images than X takes), one entry per platform. A platform without an entry uses the post mediaUrls. The entry must match the post contentType: one video for VIDEO, one image for IMAGE, one document for DOCUMENT, two or more items for CAROUSEL; TEXT posts take none. Each entry is checked against its own platform's limits only, and the post mediaUrls is no longer checked against that platform. An entry for a platform the post does not go to, an empty mediaUrls, a data URI, a second entry for one platform and media of another type are refused with 400. An overridden platform does not use the post-level thumbnailUrl or thumbnailTimestampMs; give it its own through platformThumbnails. On an update, sending the array replaces every override, [] clears them all and omitting it keeps the stored ones; it takes effect even without platforms. get_post shows an override as mediaOverrideUrls and mediaOverrideAltTexts on that platform

platform.description: The platform whose images are reframed to aspectRatio

aspectRatio.description: SQUARE is 1:1, PORTRAIT 4:5, VERTICAL 9:16 and LANDSCAPE 1.91:1

fit.description: How an image of another shape reaches the ratio. CROP (the default) cuts it from the center; PAD keeps the whole image and fills the rest with a blurred copy of it

platformAspectRatios.description: Reframe every image of an IMAGE or CAROUSEL post to one shape on a platform, one entry per platform. INSTAGRAM takes SQUARE, PORTRAIT or LANDSCAPE (Instagram refuses 9:16 feed and carousel images); TIKTOK takes all four. Video posts, Instagram stories and a second entry for the same platform are refused with 400. Omit a platform to keep its images as uploaded. On an update it applies to the mediaUrls sent in the same request

twitterKeepLinks.description: Keep links in the X text clickable. X charges over 10 times more for a post with a link, so by default every link in X text is broken (example.com becomes example. com). Only AppSumo lifetime deals can turn this on, and a kept link costs 20 credits instead of 2. true on any other plan is refused with 400; it is ignored when the X text has no link

linkedinConnectionIds.description: LinkedIn account connection IDs to post from

twitterConnectionIds.description: X (Twitter) account connection IDs to post from

instagramConnectionIds.description: Instagram account connection IDs to post from

youtubeConnectionIds.description: YouTube channel connection IDs to post from

tiktokConnectionIds.description: TikTok account connection IDs to post from

threadsConnectionIds.description: Threads account connection IDs to post from

blueskyConnectionIds.description: Bluesky account connection IDs to post from

mastodonConnectionIds.description: Mastodon account connection IDs to post from

pinterestConnectionIds.description: Pinterest account connection IDs to post from

tumblrConnectionIds.description: Tumblr blogs to post to, by the account id from list_accounts. TUMBLR takes text up to 32768 characters, up to 30 JPEG, PNG or GIF images (10 MB each) or one MP4 video (500 MB, up to 10 minutes), and alt text; it has no first comments, threads, per-platform thumbnails, image shapes or analytics

telegramConnectionIds.description: Telegram channels and groups to post to, by the account id from list_accounts. TELEGRAM takes text up to 4096 characters, up to 10 images (JPEG, PNG or WebP, 10 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (50 MB); a caption over 1024 characters goes out as its own message after the media

wordpressConnectionIds.description: WordPress sites to post to, by the account id from list_accounts. WORDPRESS publishes the text as the body of a blog post, up to 100,000 characters: blank lines start new paragraphs and bare links become clickable. It takes up to 20 JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF images (20 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (500 MB); the first image is the featured image and the other images or the video follow the text. A site without an entry in wordpressConfigs uses the first line of the text as the title. WordPress has no first comments, threads, thumbnails, image shapes or analytics

googleBusinessConnectionIds.description: Google Business Profile locations to post to, by the account id from list_accounts. A location without an entry in googleBusinessConfigs gets a STANDARD update

pageIds.description: Facebook page account ids from list_accounts (the account id; its pageId value is also accepted). Facebook has no connection-id array

title.description: On a photo post, the title shown above the description. On a video, sent as the caption only when caption is empty

caption.description: TikTok-specific caption, used instead of the post text. TikTok caps it at 2200 characters on a video; on a photo or photo carousel post it is the description and can use the full length. Falls back to title, then to the post text. A video sent with sendAsDraft can reach the TikTok inbox without it, because TikTok's inbox upload takes no caption

privacyLevel.description: Who can see the TikTok post: everyone, mutual followers, followers of the creator, or only the creator (SELF_ONLY)

allowComments.description: Allow comments on the TikTok post

allowDuet.description: Allow other users to Duet this video

allowStitch.description: Allow other users to Stitch this video

sendAsDraft.description: Save as TikTok draft so the user can add trending sounds before publishing

aiGenerated.description: Label content as AI-generated

brandedContentOwnBrand.description: Disclose as promoting your own brand

autoAddMusic.description: Let TikTok auto-add music to the video

tiktokConfigs.description: TikTok per-connection config. Each entry needs connectionId + privacyLevel at minimum

postType.description: VIDEO for long-form, SHORTS for YouTube Shorts

tags.description: Keyword tags stored on the YouTube video

privacyStatus.description: Who can watch the video: public is everyone, unlisted is anyone with the link, private is only the channel

license.description: youtube is the standard YouTube license; creativeCommon publishes the video under Creative Commons Attribution so others may reuse it

notifySubscribers.description: Notify channel subscribers about the upload

allowEmbedding.description: Allow embedding the video on other sites

madeForKids.description: Mark the video as made for kids (COPPA)

categoryId.description: Numeric YouTube video category id, as a string, such as "22" for People & Blogs

playlistId.description: Id of a playlist on this channel; the uploaded video is added to it. List the ids with list_youtube_playlists

defaultAudioLanguage.description: Language spoken in the video's original audio, as a BCP-47 tag such as en, pt-BR or es-419, so YouTube does not treat it as another language. null clears a saved value. It does not turn off YouTube's automatic dubbing

aiGenerated.description: Disclose altered or synthetic content, such as an AI voice, an AI avatar or realistic footage that was generated or edited. YouTube shows its "Altered or synthetic content" label on the video. Omit it or send false for no label

scheduleOnYouTube.description: Upload the video 48 hours before scheduledAt (at once when scheduledAt is closer), as a private video that YouTube publishes itself at scheduledAt, so the user can set up a Test & Compare (thumbnail and title A/B test) in YouTube Studio before it goes public. privacyStatus must be public or omitted (400 YOUTUBE_SCHEDULE_REQUIRES_PUBLIC), and a recurring post is refused (400 YOUTUBE_SCHEDULE_NOT_RECURRING). With a scheduledAt less than 15 minutes ahead the video uploads at scheduledAt as usual. To turn it on for a post that is already scheduled, call update_post with only id and youtubeConfigs [{ connectionId, scheduleOnYouTube: true }]. Once the video is on YouTube (youtubeScheduledVideoId is set on the platform), the post cannot be updated, unscheduled or published early (409 SCHEDULED_ON_YOUTUBE); the user edits it in YouTube Studio, or deletes the post and schedules it again. Deleting it before scheduledAt also deletes the video from YouTube

youtubeConfigs.description: YouTube per-connection config: videoTitle, tags, privacyStatus, playlistId, notifySubscribers, categoryId, madeForKids, license, allowEmbedding, aiGenerated, defaultAudioLanguage, postType (VIDEO or SHORTS) and scheduleOnYouTube (upload now as a private video that YouTube publishes at scheduledAt). Get playlistId from list_youtube_playlists for that connectionId; a playlist belongs to one channel. The video description is the post text, or the YOUTUBE entry of platformTexts

postType.description: Where the post goes: FEED works with every content type, REEL needs contentType VIDEO, STORY needs IMAGE, VIDEO or CAROUSEL (a CAROUSEL story publishes each media item as its own story, in order). Any other combination is refused with 400

shareToStory.description: Also publish the same media as a story on this account, next to the FEED or REEL post. The story shows as its own entry in platforms with postType STORY, so it succeeds, fails and retries on its own. It skips the caption, first comment, cover, collaborators, trial and audio, needs IMAGE, VIDEO or CAROUSEL, and a video must fit the story length limit (60 seconds). Ignored when postType is STORY

collaborators.description: Instagram usernames invited as collaborators (Instagram Collab). A leading @ is stripped and duplicates are dropped. Works on feed images, carousels and reels; a story or a trial reel with collaborators is refused with 400. Each collaborator gets an invite in Instagram and must accept it before the post shows on their profile

title.description: Track title, stored for display only

artist.description: Artist or creator, stored for display only

audioVolume.description: How loud the added audio plays, as a percentage of its full volume. Omit for full volume

videoVolume.description: How loud the video's own sound plays under the added audio, as a percentage of its full volume. Omit for full volume

audio.description: Music or an original sound from Instagram's audio library, added to the Reel when it is published. Needs contentType VIDEO and a postType other than STORY, and only works for accounts with supportsInstagramAudio: true in list_accounts (connected through Facebook). Find ids with search_instagram_audio

trialGraduation.description: Publish a video reel as a trial reel: Instagram shows it to non-followers first and keeps it off followers' feeds and the profile grid until it is shared. MANUAL means the account owner shares it from the Instagram app; SS_PERFORMANCE means Instagram shares it if it performs well. Only for a single video posted as a reel or feed video, never a story, image or carousel (400 otherwise). Needs a professional account Instagram has enabled for trial reels; otherwise that platform fails with a message saying so

username.description: The public Instagram username to tag

x.description: Horizontal position of the tag as a fraction of the image width, where 0 is the left edge

y.description: Vertical position of the tag as a fraction of the image height, where 0 is the top edge

userTags.description: Public Instagram accounts tagged in the media. Works on a single image, a single video (published as a Reel) or a single story; a carousel or several stories with tags is refused with 400. On a feed image every tag needs x and y; on a story they are optional, and on a video they are ignored because the person is tagged on the video as a whole. A leading @ is stripped and a repeated username keeps its first entry. If Instagram refuses a tag because the account is private or does not exist, the post goes out without its tags and instagramUntaggedUsernames in get_post lists the refused usernames

aiGenerated.description: Disclose that the post was made or edited with AI. Instagram shows its "AI info" label on the post. Works on images, carousels, reels and stories, and a story made with shareToStory carries the label too. Omit it or send false for no label

instagramConfigs.description: Instagram per-connection config: post type (FEED, REEL, STORY), shareToStory, collaborators, user tags, the AI info label, Reel audio, and trial reels

postType.description: Where the post goes: FEED works with every content type, REEL needs contentType VIDEO, STORY needs IMAGE, VIDEO or CAROUSEL (a CAROUSEL story publishes each media item as its own story, in order). Any other combination is refused with 400

shareToStory.description: Also publish the same media as a story on this page, next to the FEED or REEL post. The story shows as its own entry in platforms with postType STORY, so it succeeds, fails and retries on its own. It skips the caption, video title and text background, needs IMAGE, VIDEO or CAROUSEL, and a video must fit the story length limit (60 seconds). Ignored when postType is STORY

videoTitle.description: Title shown on the Facebook video

textFormatPresetId.description: Facebook's id for a colored text background (for example 106018623298955 is solid purple, 249307305544279 is a red to blue gradient). Only for contentType TEXT posts with no media and text up to 130 characters; anything else is refused with 400. Links in the text show without a preview. If Facebook refuses the background, the post goes out as plain text

imageLayout.description: How a post with several images shows on Facebook. GRID is a photo grid. CAROUSEL is a swipeable carousel where each image is a card with its own link, and needs 2 to 5 images, no videos, postType FEED and one carouselCards entry per image; anything else is refused with 400

link.description: The http or https URL the card opens

title.description: The card's headline. Without it Facebook uses the linked page's title

description.description: The line under the headline, such as a price or the domain. Without it Facebook uses the linked page

carouselCards.description: One card per image, in the same order as the media, used when imageLayout is CAROUSEL. Facebook only shows your image, title and description on a card whose link points to a website the Page owns; for any other link the post fails with the error Facebook returns

aiGenerated.description: Disclose that the post was made or edited with AI. Facebook shows its "AI info" label on the post. Works on every contentType VIDEO post, whatever its postType: Facebook publishes every video as a reel, and a video story carries the label too. Photos, carousels and text posts are rejected with a 400. Omit it or send false for no label

facebookConfigs.description: Facebook per-page config: post type, shareToStory, video title, text background, a grid or link carousel for several images, and the AI info label. pageId must match an entry in pageIds

aiGenerated.description: Disclose that the post contains AI-generated content. Threads shows its "AI info" label on the post. Works on text, image, video and carousel posts; on a carousel the label covers the whole post. Thread replies do not carry it. Omit it or send false for no label

threadsConfigs.description: Threads per-account options: aiGenerated adds the AI info label. connectionId must match an entry in threadsConnectionIds

boardId.description: Board id from list_pinterest_boards. Leave out boardId and boardName to pin to a public board named AdaptlyPost, created on the account the first time it is needed

boardName.description: The board's name, instead of boardId; never send both. Matched against this account's boards, exact first, then case-insensitive. A name no board has, or one several boards share, fails with 400 and never falls back to another board

boardSectionId.description: A section id of the chosen board, to pin into that section. Needs boardId or boardName. Leave out boardSectionId and boardSectionName to pin to the board itself

boardSectionName.description: The name of one of the chosen board's sections, instead of boardSectionId; never send both. Matched exact first, then case-insensitive. Fails with 400 when no section has the name, when several do (the message lists their ids), or when no board is given. No tool lists sections, so ask the user for the name

title.description: Title shown on the pin

aiGenerated.description: Disclose that the Pin was made or modified with AI. Sends Pinterest the AI_MODIFIED disclosure, which shows an "AI modified" label on the Pin. Works on image, video and carousel Pins. Omit it or send false for no label

aiGeneratedPerson.description: Disclose that the Pin shows a person generated with AI. Sends Pinterest the SYNTHETIC_PERFORMER disclosure, next to AI_MODIFIED when aiGenerated is also set. Works on image, video and carousel Pins. Omit it or send false for no disclosure

pinterestConfigs.description: Pinterest per-connection config: the board and board section to pin to, a pin title, a destination link, the AI modified label and the AI-generated person disclosure. Get boardId from list_pinterest_boards for that connectionId, or pass the board name as boardName instead (not both); a board belongs to one Pinterest account. A boardName that matches no board or several fails with 400. Without either the pin goes to a board named AdaptlyPost

connectionId.description: Google Business Profile account id from list_accounts

topicType.description: STANDARD is an update. EVENT and OFFER need eventTitle, eventStart and eventEnd

callToActionType.description: Button shown on the post. Every type except CALL needs callToActionUrl; CALL dials the phone number on the Business Profile

callToActionUrl.description: Page the button opens. Ignored when callToActionType is CALL

eventTitle.description: Title of the event or offer

eventStart.description: Start of the event or offer in the business's local time with no offset, as a date or a date and time (e.g. "2026-10-01T18:00"). Google reads event times in the location's time zone

eventEnd.description: End of the event or offer in the business's local time with no offset, as a date or a date and time (e.g. "2026-10-01T21:00")

offerRedeemUrl.description: OFFER only: where the offer is redeemed

googleBusinessConfigs.description: Google Business Profile per-location config: update, event or offer, plus a button. connectionId must match an entry in googleBusinessConnectionIds. GOOGLE_BUSINESS takes TEXT or IMAGE with one JPEG or PNG image up to 5 MB, and text up to 1500 characters

connectionId.description: Tumblr blog account id from list_accounts

tags.description: Tags shown on the Tumblr post. A leading # is stripped and duplicates are dropped, ignoring case

title.description: Shown as a heading above the media and the text

sourceUrl.description: Shown as the source link of the post

tumblrConfigs.description: Tumblr per-blog config: tags, a title and a source link. connectionId must match an entry in tumblrConnectionIds

connectionId.description: WordPress site account id from list_accounts

title.description: Post title. Defaults to the first line of the text, cut to 100 characters

excerpt.description: Summary WordPress shows in post lists and feeds

categoryIds.description: Category ids from list_wordpress_categories for this site. Omitted, WordPress files the post under the site's default category

tags.description: WordPress tag names. A tag the site does not have yet is created when the WordPress user may manage tags, and skipped otherwise

status.description: What the post becomes on the site at the post's time. PUBLISH (default) publishes it live. DRAFT leaves a WordPress draft the user finishes and publishes or schedules in WordPress. PENDING submits it for review (Pending Review). Unrelated to saveAsDraft: the post must still be published or scheduled to reach the site. For DRAFT and PENDING the post's postUrl opens it in the WordPress editor

wordpressConfigs.description: WordPress per-site config: title, excerpt, categories, tags and status (publish, leave a draft or submit for review). connectionId must match an entry in wordpressConnectionIds

documentTitle.description: Title LinkedIn shows on a DOCUMENT post. Defaults to the file name; ignored for other content types

reshareOf.description: Reshare this LinkedIn post from the account, with the post text as the commentary. Takes a urn:li:share: or urn:li:ugcPost: URN, such as the platformPostId from list_post_results, or a LinkedIn post link of the form https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/<urn>, which is also the link inside a post's Embed code. urn:li:activity: links are refused because LinkedIn cannot reshare them through its API. Media on the post is not attached on this account

linkedinConfigs.description: LinkedIn per-connection config: documentTitle names a DOCUMENT post, reshareOf reshares another LinkedIn post with the text as commentary. connectionId must match an entry in linkedinConnectionIds

quoteOf.description: Quote one of this account's own X posts, with the post text as the commentary. Takes a post link such as https://x.com/<handle>/status/<id> or the post's numeric id, such as the platformPostId from list_post_results. X only lets an account quote posts it wrote or posts that mention it: a link naming another handle is refused with 400, and any other post fails when it publishes. Needs text, and media on the post is not attached on this account. Costs the same as any X post

aiGenerated.description: Disclose that the post contains AI-generated media. Sets made_with_ai on the X post, and X labels it. Omit it or send false for no label

twitterConfigs.description: X per-connection config: quoteOf quotes one of the account's own posts with the text as commentary, aiGenerated adds the made-with-AI label. connectionId must match an entry in twitterConnectionIds

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

tools.name: validate_post
tools.title: Validate Post
tools.description: Dry-run create_post: takes exactly the same input and runs every check creating the post would run, plus the ones that usually fail only at publish time (TikTok creator limits, YouTube upload quota, expired tokens, Pinterest boards, X credits), without creating a post, uploading media or writing anything. Nothing is published, so no confirmation is needed. Always returns a report: valid is false when any issue has severity ERROR. Issues tied to one account are listed under that account in accounts (status READY, WARNING or BLOCKED); the rest are in issues, each with a stable code, severity and message. outcome says what creating the post would do (DRAFT, SCHEDULED or PUBLISH_NOW), and requiredPermissions names the permissions it would need; a missing one shows up as a PERMISSION_DENIED issue. notChecked lists what only the platform decides at publish time, so valid: true is not a guarantee. Fix every ERROR, then call create_post with the same input. Needs the posts.draft permission.

text.description: Default post text shared across platforms. On LinkedIn, mention a company page with @[Page Name](urn:li:organization:<id>), using the page name exactly as LinkedIn shows it

accountIds.description: Account ids (or Facebook pageIds) from list_accounts to post to. AdaptlyPost adds each account's platform to platforms and its id to the matching connection-id array, so you can send these instead of platforms and the per-platform arrays, or alongside them. An id not connected to the workspace fails with 400

platforms.description: Target platforms (e.g. ["LINKEDIN", "TWITTER"]). Each one needs its matching connection-id array (pageIds for FACEBOOK, googleBusinessConnectionIds for GOOGLE_BUSINESS) filled with ids from list_accounts. Optional when accountIds is sent

contentType.description: What the post carries; it must match mediaUrls. CAROUSEL takes 2 or more items in mediaUrls, up to 4 on BLUESKY and MASTODON, 5 on PINTEREST, 10 on INSTAGRAM, FACEBOOK, THREADS and TELEGRAM, 20 on TWITTER, LINKEDIN and WORDPRESS, 30 on TUMBLR and 35 on TIKTOK (JPEG or WebP photos only). INSTAGRAM and THREADS accept images and videos in the same carousel; every other platform takes images only, and YOUTUBE has no carousel. Give a platform with a lower limit its own items through platformMedia. GOOGLE_BUSINESS takes TEXT or IMAGE with one JPEG or PNG image up to 5 MB, and text up to 1500 characters. TELEGRAM takes text up to 4096 characters, up to 10 images (JPEG, PNG or WebP, 10 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (50 MB); a caption over 1024 characters goes out as its own message after the media. WORDPRESS publishes the text as the body of a blog post, up to 100,000 characters: blank lines start new paragraphs and bare links become clickable. It takes up to 20 JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF images (20 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (500 MB); the first image is the featured image and the other images or the video follow the text. DOCUMENT publishes one PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC or DOCX file (max 100 MB, 300 pages) as a LinkedIn document post and is LinkedIn only: put exactly that one file in mediaUrls, target only LINKEDIN, and set the title with linkedinConfigs

scheduledAt.description: Absolute ISO 8601 instant to schedule (e.g. "2026-03-15T10:00:00Z"). Omit to post immediately; a past time also posts immediately. With saveAsDraft it is the draft's planned date instead: nothing is scheduled, and publish_draft without a date later schedules the draft for it

timezone.description: IANA timezone stored with the post for display (e.g. "America/New_York"); it does not shift scheduledAt

saveAsDraft.description: Save as DRAFT instead of publishing or scheduling; publish later with publish_draft. A scheduledAt sent with it is stored as the draft's planned date, and publish_draft schedules the draft for that date

frequency.description: How often the post repeats. YEARLY repeats on the same date; a series started on February 29 posts on February 28 in other years

interval.description: Repeat every N periods of frequency, so 2 with WEEKLY is every other week (default 1)

weekdays.description: WEEKLY only: the weekdays it goes out on (e.g. ["MONDAY", "THURSDAY"]). The weekday of scheduledAt is always included

endsOn.description: Last day an occurrence may go out on, as YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Must be on or after the day of the first post. Cannot be combined with maxOccurrences

maxOccurrences.description: Total number of posts the series publishes. Cannot be combined with endsOn; omit both to repeat until the user pauses or deletes the series

recurrence.description: Repeat the post on a schedule the user asked for, and confirm that schedule with them first. Needs a future scheduledAt, which becomes the first post and sets the time of day in timezone. Cannot be combined with saveAsDraft or TIKTOK. Missed slots, for example while paused, are skipped and never published late. The user can pause or stop the series at any time with pause_recurring_post or delete_recurring_post; list_recurring_posts shows it

mediaUrls.description: Media URLs to attach. Use publicUrl values from upload_media or get_upload_urls; the same publicUrl may be reused across posts. Do not reuse mediaUrls read back from a published post, which may be expiring platform links

mediaAltTexts.description: Alt text per image, in the same order as mediaUrls (use "" to skip an image). Sent to X, Bluesky, Mastodon, Tumblr, WordPress, LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram and Threads; Pinterest uses the first one on image, carousel and video Pins (cut to 500). TikTok, YouTube and Google Business Profile ignore it, and so do videos on the other platforms

labelIds.description: Label IDs from list_labels to put on the post, for example one label per brand. Max 10. An ID that is not a label of the workspace returns 400. Labels organise posts inside AdaptlyPost and are never sent to a platform

thumbnailUrl.description: Video thumbnail as an https URL or an image data URI, used on every platform that takes one unless platformThumbnails overrides it

thumbnailTimestampMs.description: Video frame timestamp (ms) to use as the thumbnail on every platform that takes one: YOUTUBE, FACEBOOK, INSTAGRAM, LINKEDIN, PINTEREST, TELEGRAM and TIKTOK. A thumbnailUrl sent with it wins everywhere except TIKTOK, which takes only a frame, and platformThumbnails overrides both

platform.description: The platform that gets this text instead of the post text; one entry per platform

text.description: On LinkedIn, mention a company page with @[Page Name](urn:li:organization:<id>), using the page name exactly as LinkedIn shows it

platform.description: The platform whose published post gets this comment

text.description: The comment's text, trimmed. The limit depends on the platform, see firstComments

delayMinutes.description: How many minutes after the platform publishes to post the comment, up to 10080 (7 days). Omit it or send 0 for no delay. The comment goes out within about a minute of that time; without a delay, within about a minute of the post (about two minutes on YouTube). Once the post is published the delay cannot be changed; deleting the post cancels a comment that has not gone out yet

firstComments.description: A comment posted from the same account shortly after the post goes out on a platform, one entry per platform. Available on LINKEDIN (1250 characters), TWITTER (280, as a reply), THREADS (500, as a reply), BLUESKY (300, as a reply), MASTODON (500, as a reply), YOUTUBE (10000), FACEBOOK (8000) and INSTAGRAM (2200). A platform the post does not go to, an empty or too long comment, a second entry for one platform, a platform that also has threadReplies, a private or made for kids YouTube video and Facebook or Instagram stories are refused with 400. The comment goes out within about a minute of the platform publishing (about two minutes on YouTube), or within about a minute of delayMinutes after it when the entry sets one, and is retried up to 3 times; on X it is not retried, and a lifetime-deal account pays for it like any X post. A Facebook Page or Instagram account connected before first comments came to them must be reconnected once; until then its comment fails and firstCommentError says to reconnect. A comment that fails never fails the post: read firstCommentStatus and firstCommentError on the platform in get_post. On an update, sending the array replaces every first comment and omitting it keeps the stored ones

platform.description: The platform whose published post these replies follow

texts.description: The replies in order, each trimmed. The limit per reply depends on the platform, see threadReplies

mediaUrls.description: Parallel to texts: the JPEG, PNG, GIF or WEBP image URLs of each reply, from upload_media, and [] for a reply without images

threadReplies.description: Turns the post into a thread: the post opens it and each text is published as a reply to the one before, from the same account, one entry per platform. A reply can carry up to 4 images (JPEG, PNG, GIF or WEBP) through mediaUrls, adapted to the platform like the post's own images; a reply with images may leave its text empty. Available on TWITTER (280 characters per reply, or the account's own limit on X Premium), THREADS (500), BLUESKY (300) and MASTODON (500, or the instance's limit), up to 25 replies. A platform the post does not go to, a reply with neither text nor images, a too long reply, more than 25 replies, more than 4 images or a video on a reply, a second entry for one platform and a platform that also has a first comment are refused with 400. An entry with an empty texts array removes the thread. Replies start about 10 seconds after the platform publishes, 2 seconds apart. A failed run is retried up to 3 times and resumes after the last reply that went out; on X it is not retried, and a lifetime-deal account pays for each reply like any X post. A thread that fails never fails the post: read threadStatus, threadReplyIds and threadError on the platform in get_post. On an update, sending the array replaces every thread and omitting it keeps the stored ones

platform.description: The platform that uses this thumbnail instead of the post-level one

thumbnailUrl.description: The image to use as this platform's thumbnail, an https URL or an image data URI

thumbnailTimestampMs.description: The video frame (ms from the start) to use as this platform's thumbnail

platformThumbnails.description: A different thumbnail for one platform of a VIDEO post, one entry per platform. A platform without an entry uses the post-level thumbnailUrl and thumbnailTimestampMs. YOUTUBE, FACEBOOK, INSTAGRAM, LINKEDIN, PINTEREST and TELEGRAM take an image (thumbnailUrl) or a frame (thumbnailTimestampMs), the image winning when both are sent; TIKTOK takes only a frame. Posts that are not videos, Facebook and Instagram stories, a second entry for one platform and an entry the platform cannot use are refused with 400. On an update, sending the array replaces every override and omitting it keeps the stored ones

platform.description: The platform that publishes this media instead of the post mediaUrls

mediaUrls.description: This platform's media, publicUrl values from upload_media or get_upload_urls. Public https URLs only, no data URIs

mediaAltTexts.description: Alt text per item, in the same order as this entry's mediaUrls (use "" to skip one)

platformMedia.description: Different media for one platform, for when the post media does not fit it (a video too long for TikTok, a carousel with more images than X takes), one entry per platform. A platform without an entry uses the post mediaUrls. The entry must match the post contentType: one video for VIDEO, one image for IMAGE, one document for DOCUMENT, two or more items for CAROUSEL; TEXT posts take none. Each entry is checked against its own platform's limits only, and the post mediaUrls is no longer checked against that platform. An entry for a platform the post does not go to, an empty mediaUrls, a data URI, a second entry for one platform and media of another type are refused with 400. An overridden platform does not use the post-level thumbnailUrl or thumbnailTimestampMs; give it its own through platformThumbnails. On an update, sending the array replaces every override, [] clears them all and omitting it keeps the stored ones; it takes effect even without platforms. get_post shows an override as mediaOverrideUrls and mediaOverrideAltTexts on that platform

platform.description: The platform whose images are reframed to aspectRatio

aspectRatio.description: SQUARE is 1:1, PORTRAIT 4:5, VERTICAL 9:16 and LANDSCAPE 1.91:1

fit.description: How an image of another shape reaches the ratio. CROP (the default) cuts it from the center; PAD keeps the whole image and fills the rest with a blurred copy of it

platformAspectRatios.description: Reframe every image of an IMAGE or CAROUSEL post to one shape on a platform, one entry per platform. INSTAGRAM takes SQUARE, PORTRAIT or LANDSCAPE (Instagram refuses 9:16 feed and carousel images); TIKTOK takes all four. Video posts, Instagram stories and a second entry for the same platform are refused with 400. Omit a platform to keep its images as uploaded. On an update it applies to the mediaUrls sent in the same request

twitterKeepLinks.description: Keep links in the X text clickable. X charges over 10 times more for a post with a link, so by default every link in X text is broken (example.com becomes example. com). Only AppSumo lifetime deals can turn this on, and a kept link costs 20 credits instead of 2. true on any other plan is refused with 400; it is ignored when the X text has no link

linkedinConnectionIds.description: LinkedIn account connection IDs to post from

twitterConnectionIds.description: X (Twitter) account connection IDs to post from

instagramConnectionIds.description: Instagram account connection IDs to post from

youtubeConnectionIds.description: YouTube channel connection IDs to post from

tiktokConnectionIds.description: TikTok account connection IDs to post from

threadsConnectionIds.description: Threads account connection IDs to post from

blueskyConnectionIds.description: Bluesky account connection IDs to post from

mastodonConnectionIds.description: Mastodon account connection IDs to post from

pinterestConnectionIds.description: Pinterest account connection IDs to post from

tumblrConnectionIds.description: Tumblr blogs to post to, by the account id from list_accounts. TUMBLR takes text up to 32768 characters, up to 30 JPEG, PNG or GIF images (10 MB each) or one MP4 video (500 MB, up to 10 minutes), and alt text; it has no first comments, threads, per-platform thumbnails, image shapes or analytics

telegramConnectionIds.description: Telegram channels and groups to post to, by the account id from list_accounts. TELEGRAM takes text up to 4096 characters, up to 10 images (JPEG, PNG or WebP, 10 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (50 MB); a caption over 1024 characters goes out as its own message after the media

wordpressConnectionIds.description: WordPress sites to post to, by the account id from list_accounts. WORDPRESS publishes the text as the body of a blog post, up to 100,000 characters: blank lines start new paragraphs and bare links become clickable. It takes up to 20 JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF images (20 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (500 MB); the first image is the featured image and the other images or the video follow the text. A site without an entry in wordpressConfigs uses the first line of the text as the title. WordPress has no first comments, threads, thumbnails, image shapes or analytics

googleBusinessConnectionIds.description: Google Business Profile locations to post to, by the account id from list_accounts. A location without an entry in googleBusinessConfigs gets a STANDARD update

pageIds.description: Facebook page account ids from list_accounts (the account id; its pageId value is also accepted). Facebook has no connection-id array

title.description: On a photo post, the title shown above the description. On a video, sent as the caption only when caption is empty

caption.description: TikTok-specific caption, used instead of the post text. TikTok caps it at 2200 characters on a video; on a photo or photo carousel post it is the description and can use the full length. Falls back to title, then to the post text. A video sent with sendAsDraft can reach the TikTok inbox without it, because TikTok's inbox upload takes no caption

privacyLevel.description: Who can see the TikTok post: everyone, mutual followers, followers of the creator, or only the creator (SELF_ONLY)

allowComments.description: Allow comments on the TikTok post

allowDuet.description: Allow other users to Duet this video

allowStitch.description: Allow other users to Stitch this video

sendAsDraft.description: Save as TikTok draft so the user can add trending sounds before publishing

aiGenerated.description: Label content as AI-generated

brandedContentOwnBrand.description: Disclose as promoting your own brand

autoAddMusic.description: Let TikTok auto-add music to the video

tiktokConfigs.description: TikTok per-connection config. Each entry needs connectionId + privacyLevel at minimum

postType.description: VIDEO for long-form, SHORTS for YouTube Shorts

tags.description: Keyword tags stored on the YouTube video

privacyStatus.description: Who can watch the video: public is everyone, unlisted is anyone with the link, private is only the channel

license.description: youtube is the standard YouTube license; creativeCommon publishes the video under Creative Commons Attribution so others may reuse it

notifySubscribers.description: Notify channel subscribers about the upload

allowEmbedding.description: Allow embedding the video on other sites

madeForKids.description: Mark the video as made for kids (COPPA)

categoryId.description: Numeric YouTube video category id, as a string, such as "22" for People & Blogs

playlistId.description: Id of a playlist on this channel; the uploaded video is added to it. List the ids with list_youtube_playlists

defaultAudioLanguage.description: Language spoken in the video's original audio, as a BCP-47 tag such as en, pt-BR or es-419, so YouTube does not treat it as another language. null clears a saved value. It does not turn off YouTube's automatic dubbing

aiGenerated.description: Disclose altered or synthetic content, such as an AI voice, an AI avatar or realistic footage that was generated or edited. YouTube shows its "Altered or synthetic content" label on the video. Omit it or send false for no label

scheduleOnYouTube.description: Upload the video 48 hours before scheduledAt (at once when scheduledAt is closer), as a private video that YouTube publishes itself at scheduledAt, so the user can set up a Test & Compare (thumbnail and title A/B test) in YouTube Studio before it goes public. privacyStatus must be public or omitted (400 YOUTUBE_SCHEDULE_REQUIRES_PUBLIC), and a recurring post is refused (400 YOUTUBE_SCHEDULE_NOT_RECURRING). With a scheduledAt less than 15 minutes ahead the video uploads at scheduledAt as usual. To turn it on for a post that is already scheduled, call update_post with only id and youtubeConfigs [{ connectionId, scheduleOnYouTube: true }]. Once the video is on YouTube (youtubeScheduledVideoId is set on the platform), the post cannot be updated, unscheduled or published early (409 SCHEDULED_ON_YOUTUBE); the user edits it in YouTube Studio, or deletes the post and schedules it again. Deleting it before scheduledAt also deletes the video from YouTube

youtubeConfigs.description: YouTube per-connection config: videoTitle, tags, privacyStatus, playlistId, notifySubscribers, categoryId, madeForKids, license, allowEmbedding, aiGenerated, defaultAudioLanguage, postType (VIDEO or SHORTS) and scheduleOnYouTube (upload now as a private video that YouTube publishes at scheduledAt). Get playlistId from list_youtube_playlists for that connectionId; a playlist belongs to one channel. The video description is the post text, or the YOUTUBE entry of platformTexts

postType.description: Where the post goes: FEED works with every content type, REEL needs contentType VIDEO, STORY needs IMAGE, VIDEO or CAROUSEL (a CAROUSEL story publishes each media item as its own story, in order). Any other combination is refused with 400

shareToStory.description: Also publish the same media as a story on this account, next to the FEED or REEL post. The story shows as its own entry in platforms with postType STORY, so it succeeds, fails and retries on its own. It skips the caption, first comment, cover, collaborators, trial and audio, needs IMAGE, VIDEO or CAROUSEL, and a video must fit the story length limit (60 seconds). Ignored when postType is STORY

collaborators.description: Instagram usernames invited as collaborators (Instagram Collab). A leading @ is stripped and duplicates are dropped. Works on feed images, carousels and reels; a story or a trial reel with collaborators is refused with 400. Each collaborator gets an invite in Instagram and must accept it before the post shows on their profile

title.description: Track title, stored for display only

artist.description: Artist or creator, stored for display only

audioVolume.description: How loud the added audio plays, as a percentage of its full volume. Omit for full volume

videoVolume.description: How loud the video's own sound plays under the added audio, as a percentage of its full volume. Omit for full volume

audio.description: Music or an original sound from Instagram's audio library, added to the Reel when it is published. Needs contentType VIDEO and a postType other than STORY, and only works for accounts with supportsInstagramAudio: true in list_accounts (connected through Facebook). Find ids with search_instagram_audio

trialGraduation.description: Publish a video reel as a trial reel: Instagram shows it to non-followers first and keeps it off followers' feeds and the profile grid until it is shared. MANUAL means the account owner shares it from the Instagram app; SS_PERFORMANCE means Instagram shares it if it performs well. Only for a single video posted as a reel or feed video, never a story, image or carousel (400 otherwise). Needs a professional account Instagram has enabled for trial reels; otherwise that platform fails with a message saying so

username.description: The public Instagram username to tag

x.description: Horizontal position of the tag as a fraction of the image width, where 0 is the left edge

y.description: Vertical position of the tag as a fraction of the image height, where 0 is the top edge

userTags.description: Public Instagram accounts tagged in the media. Works on a single image, a single video (published as a Reel) or a single story; a carousel or several stories with tags is refused with 400. On a feed image every tag needs x and y; on a story they are optional, and on a video they are ignored because the person is tagged on the video as a whole. A leading @ is stripped and a repeated username keeps its first entry. If Instagram refuses a tag because the account is private or does not exist, the post goes out without its tags and instagramUntaggedUsernames in get_post lists the refused usernames

aiGenerated.description: Disclose that the post was made or edited with AI. Instagram shows its "AI info" label on the post. Works on images, carousels, reels and stories, and a story made with shareToStory carries the label too. Omit it or send false for no label

instagramConfigs.description: Instagram per-connection config: post type (FEED, REEL, STORY), shareToStory, collaborators, user tags, the AI info label, Reel audio, and trial reels

postType.description: Where the post goes: FEED works with every content type, REEL needs contentType VIDEO, STORY needs IMAGE, VIDEO or CAROUSEL (a CAROUSEL story publishes each media item as its own story, in order). Any other combination is refused with 400

shareToStory.description: Also publish the same media as a story on this page, next to the FEED or REEL post. The story shows as its own entry in platforms with postType STORY, so it succeeds, fails and retries on its own. It skips the caption, video title and text background, needs IMAGE, VIDEO or CAROUSEL, and a video must fit the story length limit (60 seconds). Ignored when postType is STORY

videoTitle.description: Title shown on the Facebook video

textFormatPresetId.description: Facebook's id for a colored text background (for example 106018623298955 is solid purple, 249307305544279 is a red to blue gradient). Only for contentType TEXT posts with no media and text up to 130 characters; anything else is refused with 400. Links in the text show without a preview. If Facebook refuses the background, the post goes out as plain text

imageLayout.description: How a post with several images shows on Facebook. GRID is a photo grid. CAROUSEL is a swipeable carousel where each image is a card with its own link, and needs 2 to 5 images, no videos, postType FEED and one carouselCards entry per image; anything else is refused with 400

link.description: The http or https URL the card opens

title.description: The card's headline. Without it Facebook uses the linked page's title

description.description: The line under the headline, such as a price or the domain. Without it Facebook uses the linked page

carouselCards.description: One card per image, in the same order as the media, used when imageLayout is CAROUSEL. Facebook only shows your image, title and description on a card whose link points to a website the Page owns; for any other link the post fails with the error Facebook returns

aiGenerated.description: Disclose that the post was made or edited with AI. Facebook shows its "AI info" label on the post. Works on every contentType VIDEO post, whatever its postType: Facebook publishes every video as a reel, and a video story carries the label too. Photos, carousels and text posts are rejected with a 400. Omit it or send false for no label

facebookConfigs.description: Facebook per-page config: post type, shareToStory, video title, text background, a grid or link carousel for several images, and the AI info label. pageId must match an entry in pageIds

aiGenerated.description: Disclose that the post contains AI-generated content. Threads shows its "AI info" label on the post. Works on text, image, video and carousel posts; on a carousel the label covers the whole post. Thread replies do not carry it. Omit it or send false for no label

threadsConfigs.description: Threads per-account options: aiGenerated adds the AI info label. connectionId must match an entry in threadsConnectionIds

boardId.description: Board id from list_pinterest_boards. Leave out boardId and boardName to pin to a public board named AdaptlyPost, created on the account the first time it is needed

boardName.description: The board's name, instead of boardId; never send both. Matched against this account's boards, exact first, then case-insensitive. A name no board has, or one several boards share, fails with 400 and never falls back to another board

boardSectionId.description: A section id of the chosen board, to pin into that section. Needs boardId or boardName. Leave out boardSectionId and boardSectionName to pin to the board itself

boardSectionName.description: The name of one of the chosen board's sections, instead of boardSectionId; never send both. Matched exact first, then case-insensitive. Fails with 400 when no section has the name, when several do (the message lists their ids), or when no board is given. No tool lists sections, so ask the user for the name

title.description: Title shown on the pin

aiGenerated.description: Disclose that the Pin was made or modified with AI. Sends Pinterest the AI_MODIFIED disclosure, which shows an "AI modified" label on the Pin. Works on image, video and carousel Pins. Omit it or send false for no label

aiGeneratedPerson.description: Disclose that the Pin shows a person generated with AI. Sends Pinterest the SYNTHETIC_PERFORMER disclosure, next to AI_MODIFIED when aiGenerated is also set. Works on image, video and carousel Pins. Omit it or send false for no disclosure

pinterestConfigs.description: Pinterest per-connection config: the board and board section to pin to, a pin title, a destination link, the AI modified label and the AI-generated person disclosure. Get boardId from list_pinterest_boards for that connectionId, or pass the board name as boardName instead (not both); a board belongs to one Pinterest account. A boardName that matches no board or several fails with 400. Without either the pin goes to a board named AdaptlyPost

connectionId.description: Google Business Profile account id from list_accounts

topicType.description: STANDARD is an update. EVENT and OFFER need eventTitle, eventStart and eventEnd

callToActionType.description: Button shown on the post. Every type except CALL needs callToActionUrl; CALL dials the phone number on the Business Profile

callToActionUrl.description: Page the button opens. Ignored when callToActionType is CALL

eventTitle.description: Title of the event or offer

eventStart.description: Start of the event or offer in the business's local time with no offset, as a date or a date and time (e.g. "2026-10-01T18:00"). Google reads event times in the location's time zone

eventEnd.description: End of the event or offer in the business's local time with no offset, as a date or a date and time (e.g. "2026-10-01T21:00")

offerRedeemUrl.description: OFFER only: where the offer is redeemed

googleBusinessConfigs.description: Google Business Profile per-location config: update, event or offer, plus a button. connectionId must match an entry in googleBusinessConnectionIds. GOOGLE_BUSINESS takes TEXT or IMAGE with one JPEG or PNG image up to 5 MB, and text up to 1500 characters

connectionId.description: Tumblr blog account id from list_accounts

tags.description: Tags shown on the Tumblr post. A leading # is stripped and duplicates are dropped, ignoring case

title.description: Shown as a heading above the media and the text

sourceUrl.description: Shown as the source link of the post

tumblrConfigs.description: Tumblr per-blog config: tags, a title and a source link. connectionId must match an entry in tumblrConnectionIds

connectionId.description: WordPress site account id from list_accounts

title.description: Post title. Defaults to the first line of the text, cut to 100 characters

excerpt.description: Summary WordPress shows in post lists and feeds

categoryIds.description: Category ids from list_wordpress_categories for this site. Omitted, WordPress files the post under the site's default category

tags.description: WordPress tag names. A tag the site does not have yet is created when the WordPress user may manage tags, and skipped otherwise

status.description: What the post becomes on the site at the post's time. PUBLISH (default) publishes it live. DRAFT leaves a WordPress draft the user finishes and publishes or schedules in WordPress. PENDING submits it for review (Pending Review). Unrelated to saveAsDraft: the post must still be published or scheduled to reach the site. For DRAFT and PENDING the post's postUrl opens it in the WordPress editor

wordpressConfigs.description: WordPress per-site config: title, excerpt, categories, tags and status (publish, leave a draft or submit for review). connectionId must match an entry in wordpressConnectionIds

documentTitle.description: Title LinkedIn shows on a DOCUMENT post. Defaults to the file name; ignored for other content types

reshareOf.description: Reshare this LinkedIn post from the account, with the post text as the commentary. Takes a urn:li:share: or urn:li:ugcPost: URN, such as the platformPostId from list_post_results, or a LinkedIn post link of the form https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/<urn>, which is also the link inside a post's Embed code. urn:li:activity: links are refused because LinkedIn cannot reshare them through its API. Media on the post is not attached on this account

linkedinConfigs.description: LinkedIn per-connection config: documentTitle names a DOCUMENT post, reshareOf reshares another LinkedIn post with the text as commentary. connectionId must match an entry in linkedinConnectionIds

quoteOf.description: Quote one of this account's own X posts, with the post text as the commentary. Takes a post link such as https://x.com/<handle>/status/<id> or the post's numeric id, such as the platformPostId from list_post_results. X only lets an account quote posts it wrote or posts that mention it: a link naming another handle is refused with 400, and any other post fails when it publishes. Needs text, and media on the post is not attached on this account. Costs the same as any X post

aiGenerated.description: Disclose that the post contains AI-generated media. Sets made_with_ai on the X post, and X labels it. Omit it or send false for no label

twitterConfigs.description: X per-connection config: quoteOf quotes one of the account's own posts with the text as commentary, aiGenerated adds the made-with-AI label. connectionId must match an entry in twitterConnectionIds

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

tools.name: get_post
tools.title: Get Post
tools.description: Get one post's full record by id: text, contentType, status, scheduledAt, timezone, and a platforms array with each target's connection, status, errorMessage, and media. Visible only within the workspace (the current one unless workspaceId names another); any other id returns "Post not found or access denied". Use this to inspect content before update_post or publish_draft. Use list_post_results instead when you only need per-platform publishing outcomes and the platformIds for retry_failed_platforms, and list_posts to find ids by status, platform, or date. Post ids come from create_post, bulk_schedule_posts, or list_posts.

id.description: Post ID from create_post, bulk_schedule_posts, or list_posts

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

tools.name: list_posts
tools.title: List Posts
tools.description: List posts in the workspace (the current one unless workspaceId names another), any status, newest first by default. Returns { posts, total, hasMore }; each post carries its status and a platforms array with per-platform status. Filters: statuses, platforms (posts targeting any of them), labelIds (posts carrying any of these labels from list_labels), and startDate/endDate, which bound scheduledAt, or createdAt for posts never scheduled. Page with offset while hasMore is true. Use this to find post ids or check what is already queued. Use get_post for one post's full record and list_post_results for one post's per-platform outcomes and retry ids.

statuses.description: Filter by status (e.g. ["SCHEDULED", "DRAFT"]); omit for all statuses

platforms.description: Filter to posts targeting any of these platforms

labelIds.description: Only posts carrying any of these labels. Label IDs come from list_labels

startDate.description: Lower bound (ISO 8601, e.g. "2026-03-01") on scheduledAt, or createdAt for posts never scheduled

endDate.description: Upper bound (ISO 8601, e.g. "2026-03-31") on scheduledAt, or createdAt for posts never scheduled

sortOrder.description: Date order of the list; newest first unless OLDEST is sent

offset.description: Posts to skip; increase by limit while hasMore is true

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

tools.name: list_labels
tools.title: List Labels
